The eleven ratings for Instalco

Instalco: a good operating recovery on a stretched balance sheet, priced for the recovery but not yet for the balance-sheet risk; the entry points are a share price near SEK 36 or a clean cash report on 11 February 2027

Investment memo for Richard, written by the Investment Analyst on 24 October 2026, the day after Instalco's Q3 2026 report. Reference price SEK 42.52 (21 October 2026). Money in SEK millions unless stated. The profit bases, the consensus brokers and the meaning of "our base" are defined in the end notes.

The decision for Richard

Instalco is not a buy at SEK 42.52. The way in is a price near SEK 36, or the Q4 report on 11 February 2027 if that report shows cash conversion and leverage repaired.

  • Why not now: the operating recovery is real but already in the price, while our FY2027 EPS is 21 percent below the consensus EPS that the market capitalises, and that consensus will be cut over the next two reports.
  • Why the setup is wrong for Richard: the probability of guidance and sell-side upgrades, which is what Richard looks for, is unusually low here for six to nine months, not unusually high.
  • What would change the call: a February report that repairs cash and leverage would move the restart of the acquisition engine back to H2 2027 and re-open the higher "engine-on" valuation multiple.

0 Summary: the key insights, implications and conclusions

The case in five steps.

What Instalco is
A founder-led attempt to restore this decentralised Nordic installer to its own 2017 to 2021 performance: the adjusted EBITA margin is moving from 6.4 percent in FY2025 back toward 8 percent. Four drivers carry the recovery: volume returning to a labour base pruned in 2024, bad debt normalising, low-priced legacy contracts rolling off, and the blending-in of a German platform (Fabri) that earns a 12 percent margin.
What Q3 2026 showed
The Q3 2026 report, published on 23 October, proved the operating half of the case ahead of plan and broke the balance-sheet half (the figure below gives the thresholds and the printed figures).
What the price assumes
The shares, up 63 percent in twelve months, trade at the stock's own ten-year median multiple of consensus earnings. That price pays for the operating half and assumes that the balance-sheet half will follow.
Where we differ
Our base FY2027 EPS is SEK 2.39 against the brokers' SEK 3.01. About 60 percent of that gap sits below EBITA (interest, minorities and tax) and the rest in an EBITDA about 5 percent lower; the whole gap sits behind a leverage gate that has moved out by a year.
What comes next
The next six months should bring operating beats, EPS cuts and unchanged guidance. The re-rating branch, in which the acquisition engine restarts and the shares earn an "engine-on" multiple, now opens in 2028 rather than 2027, and only if the February 2027 cash report reverses Q3.

The seven insights that matter most.

  1. The margin recovery is real, and it is running faster than both our model and the market's Swedish path. Swedish segment EBITA rose from SEK 105m (a 5.0 percent margin) in Q3 2025 to SEK 179m (7.4 percent) in Q3 2026, which is seasonally the second-weakest quarter of the year; the lead broker's path has Sweden reaching 7.2 percent only for the whole of 2027. The incremental margin on Swedish organic revenue was about 20 percent in the quarter. Swedish volume is secure for the next two quarters: the Swedish order backlog is up 16.1 percent, metropolitan projects are in execution, and Bravida Sweden reported +9 percent organic growth on the same day.
  2. Instalco's cash problem has moved from "timing" to "structure", in the Chief Financial Officer's own words. Through Q2 2026 the company blamed weak cash on late invoicing and pointed to unchanged overdue receivables. In Q3 the Chief Financial Officer described longer payment terms on a growing industrial mix as a structural shift; contract assets rose to SEK 1,004m (SEK 551m a year earlier), and working capital reached 4.0 percent of sales against 1.6 percent at year-end 2025. Bravida reported SEK 800m of operating cash flow and 110 percent cash conversion on the same morning, so Instalco's cash problem is company-specific. The research's "false friend" pattern (headline growth masking cash strain), which earlier analyses weighted at one in three, is now the most likely shape of the next two quarters; only the Q4 working-capital release, reported in February 2027, can disprove it.
  3. The 2.5x leverage gate has moved from Q4 2026 to Q4 2027, and the restart of the acquisition engine has moved with it. Net debt rose by about SEK 1.2bn in one quarter, from four sources: the SEK 393m paid for the 51 percent Fabri stake, Fabri's own debt and leases consolidated, SEK 200m of minority buy-outs, and negative operating cash flow. Reaching 2.5x pro forma by end-2027 requires roughly SEK 450m of net debt reduction on top of EBITDA growth, which our base only just achieves. Management said on 23 October that deleveraging comes before bolt-on acquisitions. We therefore remove Nordic bolt-ons from FY2027 and date their restart to 2028. That change takes about SEK 0.05 off FY2028 EPS; more importantly, it keeps the valuation in the "engine-off" band (10 to 12x EV/EBITA, on the lead broker's own framing) for another year.
  1. FY2027 consensus EPS rests on the two brokers with the lightest interest, minority and tax assumptions, and it will be cut. The FY2027 consensus of SEK 3.01 is the median of three brokers, so the two brokers with the lighter below-EBITA charges set it. Consensus assumes net financial items falling to about SEK 159m to 171m, although the Riksbank is raising rates and Q3 external interest already annualises at SEK 144m before Fabri's full debt and before the expected November hike. It assumes minorities of SEK 86m, although the nine-month minority charge is already SEK 50m with only one month of Fabri included. It assumes tax of 21 to 22 percent. Nordea has the lowest revenue and EBITDA of the three brokers and the highest EPS; Pareto has the reverse, with EPS of SEK 2.55, within 7 percent of our SEK 2.39. We expect FY2027 consensus EPS to fall 10 to 15 percent by the Q1 2027 report while consensus sales and EBITDA are held or nudged up. That pattern is the opposite of the setup Richard looks for.
  1. At SEK 42.52 the price pays the stock's ten-year median multiple on consensus earnings, but the 75th percentile on our earnings. The shares trade on 13.1x consensus 24-month-forward EPS (SEK 3.28; the 46th percentile of the stock's ten-year range) and on about 16.3x our SEK 2.61. The dashboard's guideline fair multiple of 19.93x (the ten-year 90th percentile, assigned to the "Reinforcing" phase) was reached only in 2020 and 2021, with interest rates at zero, the acquisition engine buying SEK 1bn of sales a year and growth of 25 to 36 percent. That multiple is the wrong anchor for an installer levered 2.9x whose acquisition engine is off. Our fair multiple is 14x: the 13.3x ten-year median, with a one-third weight on the 16.5x "defendable" band to credit the German growth runway. On our earnings, 14x gives a return of roughly 5 percent a year over eighteen months and 9 percent a year over three years, against total returns of 50 percent and 76 percent over the same periods at the guideline multiple.
  2. The spring 2027 wage round is the one dated negative that nobody has quantified, and Bravida has just shown which installers are protected from it. Bravida builds indexation into all its long-term contracts and reports no shortage of blue-collar workers. Instalco has not disclosed its indexed share; 43 percent of its order book is fixed-price, and contracts on the Swedish AB 04 standard contract terms carry no automatic indexation. Our base takes 40 basis points (SEK 70m) off the FY2027 margin for a 3 percent wage settlement. A settlement nearer SEB's 8 percent minimum-wage figure, applied broadly, would double that hit.
  3. The real asymmetry runs opposite to the recent share-price action. The operating business is skewed to the upside against our model: Sweden could deliver a margin of 7.5 percent or more for the year, and Fabri's first month ran at 12 percent. The per-share and balance-sheet lines are skewed to the downside against the market's model. Because Instalco's multiple is company-driven (88 percent of its share-price movement over six months was idiosyncratic), both skews pass straight through to the share price. For a buyer today the downside skew dominates for six to nine months. The constructive reading is that the entry point is dated and specific: either the February 2027 report, with rolling cash conversion back above 90 percent and a Q4 working-capital release of SEK 400m or more, or a price near SEK 36.

The five judgements that move the shares most over one to two years, with the arithmetic. The arithmetic uses about 270m shares, a 23.5 percent FY2027 tax rate and our FY2027 base EPS of SEK 2.39.

The model changes we made after Q3, and their effect on our EPS path, are set out in Appendix A.

▦ Scorecard: the twelve topics

1 Tailwinds in the operating environment, and the absence of headwinds

The Nordic volume recovery is genuine, about a year old and backed by twelve to eighteen months of order backlog, but it is now running into a rate-hiking cycle that hits Instalco's financing costs before it hits Instalco's customers.

Evidence. The Swedish building cycle has turned, and the turn now shows in installers' revenue, not just in leading indicators.

Inference and so-what. Sweden's H2 2026 organic growth rates are flattered by trough comparatives and will roughly halve from Q1 2027. The underlying growth slope is mid-single digits, of which about 3 points is cost inflation passed through to customers.

The strongest tailwind for Instalco's margin, relief in tender pricing, is about two-thirds borrowed from the data-centre work that absorbs Bravida's and Assemblin Caverion's capacity. That data-centre work is externally financed and sits inside the artificial-intelligence credit cycle. If those projects slipped, the competitors' technicians would return to ordinary tenders within two quarters, and Instalco's pricing relief would go with them.

The strongest headwind, rising interest rates, hits Instalco first through its financing costs and its valuation multiple, and only second through demand.

Where I differ from the market. The market reads Sweden's 15 percent organic growth as a demand inflection and treats the Swedish recovery as the whole thesis. I read the 15 percent as easy comparatives plus a utilisation catch-up, in a market still about 15 percent below normal volume, with the Riksbank setting the demand slope from 2027. We agree on direction for two quarters. I am below the sell-side on 2027 organic growth (5 percent against 6 to 8 percent) and would not extrapolate the Swedish growth rate past the Q1 2027 report.

Counter-case and what changes my view. The best counter-case is that Swedish volume has two to three more years to run. If the lead broker is right that the market is about 15 percent below normal volume, installers have two to three more years of volume before pricing tightens, and the Riksbank may pause if housing stalls. Double-digit organic growth in the Swedish segment in Q2 2027, against the +8.4 percent of Q2 2026, would move me toward that view.

Score: 58. A genuine, broad Nordic volume turn with a public-sector floor, capped by a rate path that hits this levered company before it hits its customers.

2 Internally driven corporate change forces, and the absence of problems

Instalco's internal change programme is the strongest half of the case, and Q3 strengthened it; but the programme restores the old company rather than transforming it, and its growth engine is switched off until leverage allows.

Evidence. Five internal forces are acting at once, and three of them have now produced measurable outputs for five consecutive quarters.

Inference and so-what. The margin method works, and it worked in a quarter the sell-side expected to be merely good.

Management has raised nothing. The five financial targets stand; no date has been given for the 8 percent margin (on 23 October management said the company is "some way from" it); and the only numerical guidance, the dividend, was cut last year.

The programme is a restoration with new controls, not a transformation. Its growth engine, bolt-on acquisitions bought at 3 to 6x EV/EBITA, is explicitly off until leverage allows, and the Q3 balance sheet has pushed that point out to end-2027.

The 8 percent group margin: consensus has it in 2028; we have it in 2030.

Where I differ from the market. The market gives the founder's urgency the benefit of the doubt on when the 8 percent margin arrives; I do not. Sweden may reach 8 percent earlier, but Norway, Finland and the wage round hold the group back to 2030. On the controls, I am more positive than the research, whose verdict is that the turnaround is "heroic, not gravitational" (driven by effort rather than self-sustaining). Five quarters of margin improvement through a reorganisation and a cash squeeze are evidence that the control system is beginning to sustain itself.

Counter-case and what changes my view. Norway's Q3 losses are the decentralised model's characteristic failure: a subsidiary problem arriving while management's attention is on Sweden. A second Norwegian write-down, or a named cluster of departures among subsidiary chief executives, would show that the new baseline of standards is not yet a control system. A dated plan for the 8 percent margin, or a capital markets day after the February report, would raise this score.

Score: 70. Among the stronger internal change sets in listed European industrials, with the growth engine deliberately switched off and now gated for a year longer.

3 Value chain and industry structure; business model and barriers; financial profile; management

Instalco is a good operating business with a real but static relational moat, attached to a leaky, levered holding structure in which about half of adjusted EBITA goes to interest, minorities and tax before it reaches shareholders.

Evidence. The four lenses show a low-margin industry, a sound decentralised model, a weakened balance sheet and a founder-dependent management team.

LensEvidence
IndustryA fragmented, local service, limited by the supply of skilled labour. Pricing is pro-cyclical and set by the utilisation of the many small firms. Wholesalers are concentrated. Instalco is third in Sweden and fourth in the Nordics; Bravida and Assemblin Caverion are two to three times its size.
Business modelAbout 150 founder-run subsidiaries keep their own brands. 80 percent of customers are repeat customers (a figure the research could not verify). Subsidiaries bid in clusters. 57 percent of the order book is cost-plus or partnering work.
Financial profileStrong cash characteristics: capital expenditure of 0.7 percent of sales and free cash flow above net income in normal years, with an 8 percent-plus margin for five years to 2021. Weakened since: return on capital employed has halved, goodwill exceeds equity, leverage is 3.3x, the FY2025 tax rate was 28 percent, and "non-recurring" items have appeared every year since 2023.
ManagementA founder-operator with a proven playbook at Instalco, Green Landscaping and Eltel. Chief Financial Officer Christina Kassberg had a good working-capital record until 2026. The country management tier has been rebuilt. The founder has no deputy, and the Head of M&A has left without a visible replacement.

Inference and so-what. Instalco's moat is relational and real, but it is not widening. The relational moat is why the group earned 8 percent margins when peers earned 5.5 percent. But Bravida's purchasing platform, its 5D design tools and its SEK 1bn automation business, and Assemblin Caverion's data-centre unit, are capabilities Instalco lacks; Instalco's nearest equivalents, Intec and Inmatiq, are small.

The industry structure supports a margin recovery driven by utilisation, not one driven by price. Instalco's margin ceiling is therefore its own history, not the higher margins of SPIE or Burkhalter.

The holding structure leaks. Interest, minorities and tax take about 45 to 50 percent of adjusted EBITA (measured before amortisation) before it reaches the shareholder.

Management is both the strongest foundation of the case and its biggest concentration risk.

Where I differ from the market. The sell-side's "compounder" framing borrows Bravida's structural story (data centres, service mix and cash) for a company that has none of the three. The research is right that Instalco's digital gap does not matter in the near term, but the gap sets a lower margin ceiling than the market's multiple implies. On management, I agree with the market on direction and discount the pace by about a year.

Counter-case and what changes my view. Fabri could give Instalco a second compounding leg that the industry analysis under-weights. Fabri's deal structure (staged, conditional on hurdles, with the founders locked in) is the best-designed element in the file, and Germany's market is five times the size of the Nordic market. If German bolt-ons can be bought at Nordic multiples and Fabri holds margins of 11 percent or more, the model has that second leg. A disclosed procurement or back-office programme with a quantified target would also raise my judgement on whether Instalco's competitive advantage is widening.

Score: 50. A mid-sized consolidator with a relational moat and a capable founder, in an industry that denies tender pricing power, with a below-average balance sheet and a leaky earnings chain.

4 Conservative guidance; keeping the sell-side conservative; the record of delivery and upgrades

Instalco gives no guidance to beat and has no mechanism for upgrading itself; the sell-side has done the upgrading, and its per-share forecasts are above ours, with the first cuts due at the next two reports.

Evidence. Instalco gives no annual guidance, only five undated through-cycle targets, and after Q3 it meets only one of them. FY2025 missed three of the five, and the dividend was cut last year.

  • Management's informal commentary is candid, and it confirms direction without giving dates. Legacy contracts are "diminishing over several quarters"; Finland's 12 percent margin was "exceptionally high"; and the cash weakness is "structural" because of the industrial mix.
  • The delivery record is cyclical: beats in recoveries, misses in downturns. Q4 2025 and Q1, Q2 and Q3 2026 all beat on the operating lines; Q3 2025, FY2024 and FY2025 missed; and cash missed in each of the last two quarters.
  • The sell-side has already raised the later years. Consensus FY2026 EPS was cut 15 percent over twelve months, and the cutting ended in Q1 2026. FY2027 and FY2028 consensus EPS have been raised 8 percent over six months, and target prices 24 percent. The buy share is 86 percent after Nordea moved to Hold on 19 October.

Inference and so-what. Instalco does not upgrade; it reiterates its targets and then meets or misses them. The sell-side has done the upgrading on the company's behalf, more through target multiples than through earnings.

The 8 percent margin target is already in consensus for 2028. Delivering it on time therefore earns the shares nothing, and delivering it late costs them.

The brokers' operating lines are credible; their below-EBITA lines are not. The brokers' revenue and EBITDA are within 2 to 5 percent of ours. The Q3 report gave the first hard evidence against their below-EBITA lines: external interest of SEK 36m in the quarter, minorities of SEK 14m in a seasonally weak quarter, and leverage of 3.3x.

We expect FY2026 consensus EPS to settle around SEK 2.10 to 2.20, and FY2027 consensus EPS to be cut 10 to 15 percent by April 2027, while consensus EBITDA is held.

Where I differ from the market. The dashboard grades sell-side earnings momentum A (snapshot of 21 October 2026), but that A comes from target prices and ratings, not from earnings. Over twelve months, FY2027 consensus EPS is up 3 percent while FY2027 consensus EBITDA is up 12 percent. That divergence is our below-EBITA argument, already visible in the sell-side's own revisions. I expect the grade to fall to B or C by mid-2027.

Counter-case and what changes my view. If Sweden delivers a margin of 7.5 percent or more for FY2026, and again in the seasonal low of Q1 2027, FY2027 EBITDA upgrades of 3 to 4 percent could roughly offset the below-EBITA cuts and hold FY2027 EPS near SEK 2.9. A dated commitment to the 8 percent margin after a clean February cash report would be the company's first genuine guidance event in years.

Score: 35. No guidance, a cyclical delivery record, and a consensus whose per-share lines are above ours with the first cuts due at the next two prints.

5 Pricing power, operating leverage, financial leverage, cost-out scope and feedback loops

Instalco's operating leverage is strong but temporary and comes from utilisation, not price; its financial leverage nearly doubles any downside at the EPS line; and the capital loop that built the company is broken until 2028.

Evidence. Of the five levers, only operating leverage is working, and it is already starting to fade.

LeverEvidenceReading
Pricing powerThe margin fell from 8.2 to 5.9 percent through the last inflation, which implies zero real price increases. The company cannot separate price from volume across 6,000 projects; public buyers award on lowest price; the indexed share of contracts is undisclosed.None demonstrable
Operating leverageThe incremental adjusted EBITA margin on Swedish organic revenue was about 10 percent in Q2 2026 and about 20 percent in Q3. Headcount is being rebuilt (6,298 at Q2 2026, against an FY2025 average of 6,042), which marks the start of the fade.Strong, temporary
Financial leverageNet financial items absorbed about 17 percent of adjusted EBITA in FY2025 and about 22 percent in our FY2026. A 100 basis-point rise in rates costs SEK 0.11 of EPS.Working against
Cost-out scopeThe 2024 closures are already in the base. Bad-debt normalisation, worth about 40 basis points, is two-thirds done. Pooling back offices across 150 subsidiaries is worth perhaps 15 to 30 basis points from 2029.Little left
Feedback loopsThe capital loop (margin, then cash, then leverage, then acquisitions, then growth and multiple) built the company. Its second link, from margin to cash, broke in Q3.Broken until 2028

Inference and so-what. Revenue growth will produce outsized EBITA growth for about four more quarters, through utilisation rather than price. In our base, adjusted EBITA grows 21 percent in FY2026 and 18 percent in FY2027 on revenue growth of 11 and 12 percent. That amplification fades toward the group margin from 2028, as hiring catches up with the backlog.

Below EBITA, the amplification is used up. Minorities of SEK 125m to 135m a year with Fabri, a heavier interest line and a higher tax mix hold adjusted EPS growth to roughly 1.1 to 1.2 times EBITA growth.

Financial leverage works in reverse with the same force. A stall into the rate hikes (flat organic growth, a 6.5 percent margin and rates 100 basis points higher) gives FY2027 EPS of about SEK 1.70: a 17 percent EBITA shortfall becomes a 29 percent EPS shortfall.

The reinforcing capital loop will not close in 2027; on our base it closes in 2028, at about 60 percent of its old pace.

Where I differ from the market. The sell-side models the acquisition engine restarting in H2 2026 to 2027 at the historical pace of SEK 800m of acquired sales a year, with net financial items falling by a third. I model a restart in 2028 at SEK 300m to 550m of acquired sales a year, with financial items flat to rising. The market treats the high incremental margin as persistent; I treat it as a utilisation effect that fades once backlog per employee stops rising.

Counter-case and what changes my view. Sweden's Q3 incremental margin of about 20 percent suggests the fade may come later than we model and the 2027 Swedish margin may exceed our 7.2 percent. That would be worth SEK 0.10 to 0.15 of FY2027 EPS and would partly offset the below-EBITA chain. A Swedish segment margin above 7.5 percent in a quarter with organic growth under 5 percent (Q1 2027 is the first candidate) would be the first evidence of real pricing discipline, and I would then add price increases to the model.

Score: 48. Strong but temporary utilisation leverage and no pricing power, with financial leverage that doubles the downside and a capital loop now a year from closing.

6 Forecast financials: scope for double-digit growth and for higher growth and margins than the past

Double-digit growth exists only at the EPS line, at about 15 percent a year to FY2030, carried by the margin recovery and Fabri; the 8 percent margin is a return to the company's best, reached in 2030, two years after consensus.

Inference. The scope for double-digit growth is at the EPS line, at about 15 percent a year compound from FY2025 to FY2030. The margin recovery and Fabri carry that growth, not revenue: revenue grows at about 8 percent a year compound, against 16 percent a year over FY2019 to FY2025.

Margins will be higher than in the last four years but not higher than in 2017 to 2021. The 8 percent margin is a return to the company's best; we have the group reaching it in 2030, two years after consensus, with price increases contributing nothing.

Reported EPS runs about SEK 0.45 to 0.55 below adjusted EPS, because of amortisation of acquired intangibles (about SEK 150m to 160m a year) and recurring "items affecting comparability" (about SEK 50m). The 30 percent payout policy applies to reported EPS, which is why our dividend path sits below consensus in FY2026 and FY2027.

The margin bridge from FY2025 to FY2028 adds about 130 basis points, and none of it comes from price. Utilisation is the largest step (+60 basis points), followed by bad-debt normalisation and Fabri's higher margin (+40 each) and the roll-off of legacy contracts (+30); the 2027 wage round (-40 net) and the cost of the country organisation and Norway (-20) offset part of the gain. Of the SEK 490m EBITA uplift, roughly 45 percent comes from Swedish utilisation and volume, which depend on one macro variable. Four below-EBITA lines, each independent of the operating recovery, then dilute the EPS uplift.

Where I differ from the market. We are within 1 to 5 percent of the three brokers on revenue and EBITDA, but 10, 21 and 22 percent below them on EPS for FY2026, FY2027 and FY2028. The FY2027 consensus of SEK 3.01 is effectively our bull case: an 8 percent margin in 2027, financial items falling to SEK 200m and a 22 percent tax rate give about SEK 2.95.

Counter-case and what changes my view. The upside branch is operating. A Swedish margin of 7.6 percent in FY2027 (the Q3 run-rate) and a normal Q4 2026 working-capital release would take FY2027 EPS to about SEK 2.55 and bring the acquisition restart back to H2 2027. The full historical bolt-on pace of SEK 800m a year from 2028 would add 2 to 3 points of growth and about SEK 0.08 of EPS a year. The downside branch is the lower third of the FY2027 EPS range (SEK 1.70 to 2.15; see Section 9): a stall into the rate hikes, a wage round absorbed on fixed-price work, or a write-down cluster.

Score: 62. Double-digit EPS growth for five years on a demonstrated margin mechanism, but a recovery to the company's own ceiling rather than a new level, and with revenue growth half its history until the engine restarts.

7 Scope for upgrades to guidance, sell-side estimates and the narrative over 6 to 12 months

Over the next three reports, a cut to FY2027 consensus EPS is four times as likely as a raise; the one favourable surprise, acquired revenue growth, is a 2028 story.

Evidence. None of the three sources of upgrades (guidance, sell-side estimates and the narrative) offers upside before 2028.

  • Guidance cannot be raised in the ordinary sense, because there is none. On 23 October management again declined to date the 8 percent margin. The dividend is the only number that moves, and with leverage at 3.3x and a stated priority on deleveraging, a dividend of SEK 0.50 again in February is now more likely than the SEK 0.70 in consensus.
  • Sell-side FY2027 EPS of SEK 3.01 is set by the two models with the lightest below-EBITA charges (Section 0). Two further points weaken it. The lead broker's financial line (SEK 159m in 2027) assumes rate cuts, while the same broker's macro desk forecasts hikes. The Q3 working-capital build pushes the acquisition restart, and the acquired growth in the brokers' models, further out.
  • The market articulates well the dynamics we agree with, and leaves out the four dynamics where we sit below it. As a result, the next negative surprises will arrive without a frame the market already uses to interpret them.

Inference and so-what. Over the next three reports I put the probability of a cut of more than 5 percent to FY2027 consensus EPS at 60 percent, a hold at 25 percent and a raise at 15 percent. The cut is most likely 10 to 15 percent, landing at two reports: the Q4 2026 report, when the brokers roll forward with the full below-EBITA run-rate and the dividend, and the Q1 2027 report, with its hard comparatives and the wage round.

Sales and EBITDA consensus should be held or nudged up 1 to 3 percent on the Swedish beats. Target prices should be held, because they are set on EV/EBITA (13x 2027 at the lead broker). A second Hold rating, from Pareto (the broker nearest our EPS), is more likely than an upgrade from Nordea.

The favourable gap is later and specific. No broker carries the acquisition restart in its revenue line, so FY2028 to FY2029 revenue is the one line on which the market will be surprised upward if the engine runs. Nor does anyone articulate a balance sheet at about 1.9x by 2029 while buying SEK 500m of sales a year.

Where I differ from the market. The market expects the Q3 beat to carry into upgrades; I expect it to carry into EBITDA holds and EPS cuts. This is the most important disagreement in the memo for a holder with a 6 to 12 month horizon.

Counter-case and what changes my view. A February report with rolling cash conversion above 100 percent, a Q4 working-capital release of SEK 450m or more and pro forma leverage at or below 2.7x would re-open the acquisition restart for H2 2027 and could lead to a capital markets day. I put that combination at about one in four. It would turn the narrative from "cash" back to "compounder" and, through EBITDA upgrades, hold FY2027 EPS near SEK 2.9.

Score: 30. The per-share consensus is more likely to be cut than met at each of the next three events, the only numerical guidance (the dividend) is more likely to disappoint than beat, and the upside line (acquired growth) is a 2028 story.

9 Riskiness and simplicity of the forecasts and expectations

The case is simple to state but hard to predict on the lines that set the share price, and its correlated roll-up risks (write-down, cash, leverage and dilution) are now live rather than latent.

Simplicity. The case is simple to state: one segment's margin, and one cash ratio that sets one leverage number, which gates one acquisition engine. Each element can be traced in reported figures: the margin in Sweden's segment line, cash in the company's own conversion and leverage figures, and the engine in the acquisitions line.

Several important inputs cannot be traced from outside: award margins on new contracts; the fixed-price and indexed shares of the backlog; subsidiary-level write-downs until they become closures; Fabri's standalone results (reported inside a merged segment, one month in arrears); the credit facility's fixed-floating mix and margin grid; and the formulas of the Fabri options.

Fragilities and requirements. Three things must hold for our base to be delivered:

  1. Swedish volume continues into the rate hikes. This is one macro variable acting through one segment and one mechanism, and it carries about 45 percent of the EBITA uplift.
  2. The Q4 2026 working-capital release matches the Q4 2025 release of SEK 451m, despite a customer mix that the Chief Financial Officer now calls structural.
  3. No cluster of fixed-price contracts fails while 43 percent of the book is un-indexed and a wage round lands. Norway's Q3 losses are the warning.

Our FY2027 EPS range runs from SEK 1.70 to 2.95 around our base of SEK 2.39, with about 30 percent of the probability below SEK 2.15 and 25 percent above SEK 2.65. Consensus at SEK 3.01 sits above the whole range; only the top decile of outcomes comes close to it.

Sector precedents. Installers underperform through four failure modes, and Instalco carries the ingredients of two. The first is late-discovered fixed-price write-downs (Caverion EUR 59m, Eltel EUR 55m, and Instalco Norway in 2021 and again now). The second is the "false friend" roll-up (Fasadgruppen: 32 percent revenue growth on 1 percent organic growth, margins halved, leverage up to 5.3x, then a rights issue). Instalco differs from Fasadgruppen in that it stopped buying, cut the dividend and has organic growth of 8 percent; it resembles Fasadgruppen in a cash conversion of 74 percent at 3.3x leverage in a hiking cycle.

The historical base rate cuts both ways. Of nine decentralised groups that lost two to three points of margin, five regained them over two to three years (SPIE, Caverion, Bravida Denmark, Nimlas Sweden and Instalco itself), through controls, service mix and indexation, in that order; two failed on cash and leverage.

Where I differ from the market. The market scores this case on the Swedish margin, which is the predictable part; I score it on cash and on the chain below EBITA, which are not predictable. After Q3 I put the probability that cash conversion stays below 100 percent through 2027 at about one in two, up from one in three before the Q3 report.

What changes my view. The February report decides the risk profile. Rolling cash conversion at or above 90 percent, with a Q4 working-capital release above SEK 400m, would take the dilution tail back under 10 percent and the cash probability back to one in three. Conversion under 80 percent, or receivables overdue by more than three months above SEK 95m, would move the case toward the bear case.

Score: 38. Simple to state and poorly predictable on the lines that set the price, with correlated roll-up risks (write-down, cash, leverage, dilution) that are now live rather than latent.

10 Where the stock is in its lifecycle

The stock is stalling inside an up-phase: Reinforcing on its operating thesis, stalled on its balance sheet, and one event in February 2027 decides which phase comes next.

The dashboard's rule places the stock in the Reinforcing phase (two-year-forward multiple of 13.1x on 23 October; momentum readings B, A and B). My read is that the operating thesis is reinforcing while the balance-sheet thesis has just stalled, so this is a stall inside an up-phase rather than a clean Reinforcing phase.

The evidence for Reinforcing is real: five consecutive operating beats, margin and organic growth both above plan, target prices and ratings rising, and the multiple back from the 7.9x trough of early 2026 to the ten-year median.

The evidence against is that the phase after Reinforcing is Broadening, in which the thesis extends to new legs (cash, the acquisition engine and Germany), and Q3 closed two of those three legs for a year. Conversion fell to 74 percent, leverage rose to 3.3x, and management ranked deleveraging ahead of bolt-ons. The one leg that did broaden, Fabri at a 12 percent margin in its first month, leaks 49 percent of its profit to minorities and is reported inside Finland's declining segment.

The sell-side cycle is the tell. Estimates for the operating lines are rising while the per-share estimates are about to be cut, which is the signature of a Reinforcing phase about to turn into Stalling on the line the market prices.

So-what. A stock that is Reinforcing but stalling earns a prudent-to-defendable multiple, not a mania multiple. Its next phase will be decided by one event, the February 2027 cash and leverage report, rather than by trend. If February passes, the stock resumes Broadening with the acquisition restart as the 2028 chapter; if February fails, the stock stalls at a lower multiple, with the "false friend" narrative attached and the research's dilution tail live.

Where I differ from the market. The dashboard's rule and the sell-side's A grade read the price and target-price momentum as a confirmed Reinforcing phase. I weight the output that broke (cash) above the outputs that confirmed the thesis (margin and growth), because the lifecycle of a roll-up turns on cash, not on margin.

Score: 50. Mid-cycle: operating momentum that would merit a Reinforcing reading, held back by a balance-sheet leg that has gone backwards and a per-share estimate cycle about to turn down.

11 The fair multiple

Our fair multiple is 14x two-year-forward EPS; the 19.9x guideline multiple belongs to the 2020 to 2021 mania and is not reachable while the acquisition engine is off.

The guideline and the ranges. The Viewforth guideline for the Reinforcing phase is 19.93x two-year-forward EPS, the 90th percentile of the stock's ten-year history. Today the shares trade on 13.1x consensus EPS and about 16.3x our EPS: the 46th percentile of ten years, but the 90th percentile of two years (the two-year median is 10.3x). Bravida trades on 16.5x (the 71st percentile of its own history), and the sector median is about 11.7x.

The lead broker frames the multiple by the state of the acquisition engine: 10 to 12x EV/EBITA with the engine off (leverage above target and acquisitions paused), 13 to 14.5x with the engine on, and a historical average of 14 to 14.5x. Its target price uses 13x 2027 EV/EBITA.

My view: 14x is the fair two-year-forward multiple for the next eighteen months, with 13.3x the centre of the plausible range and 16.5x its top; 19.9x is not reachable in this phase. The reasons, in order:

  1. The 19.9x band was earned only in 2020 to 2021, when the acquisition engine was buying SEK 1.1bn to 1.7bn of sales a year, growth was 25 to 36 percent, rates were zero and the multiple ran from 20x to a 38x peak. In the engine-on, 8 percent-margin years of 2017 to 2019, the stock traded at 10 to 15x. The phase rule therefore maps "Reinforcing" to a band that this company reached only in a mania.
  2. The acquisition engine is off and now gated to 2028, so the lead broker's engine-off band applies for most of the horizon. A 13.3x P/E is roughly consistent with the lead broker's 13x EV/EBITA target.
  3. Instalco is a Swedish small cap levered 2.9x, in a hiking cycle, in a market regime that the weekly digest describes as refusing to reward leverage or re-ratings. That combination is a reason to sit below the median multiple, not above it.
  4. Against this, the German runway and a Swedish margin running ahead of plan justify a one-third weight on the 16.5x "defendable" band, which is where Bravida trades: 16.5 × 1/3 + 13.3 × 2/3 = about 14.4x, rounded down to 14x to allow for the risk in the February cash report.
  5. Instalco's multiple is company-driven, so it will move to the engine-on band without the sector's help if February passes and a first bolt-on follows. I put the odds of that branch over eighteen months at about one in four after Q3, down from one in three before it.
Where I differ from the market. The market pays the stock's own-history median multiple for consensus earnings; on our earnings, that price is the 75th percentile. Either the market is right on EPS and the multiple is fair, or the market is right on EBITDA but wrong on the chain below it, in which case it is paying a defendable-band multiple for a stock whose acquisition engine is off. I think the second is true.

What changes my view. A February report that passes both the cash and the leverage tests, together with a dated plan for the 8 percent margin, would move my central multiple to 15 to 16x. A de-rating of Bravida (whose data-centre backlog is externally financed) would remove the 16.5x anchor and move my central multiple toward 13x.

Score: 40. The stock trades at or above its fair multiple on our earnings and below it only on consensus earnings that are about to be cut; the guideline band is a 2020 to 2021 artefact for a company with its engine off.

12 Total shareholder return, Dupont framework

At our fair 14x the most likely return is about 5 percent a year over eighteen months; only a price near SEK 36 makes the 20 percent-a-year bar reachable on our earnings.

The model's return at the guideline multiple (19.93x). The Financial Analyst's model shows +53.9 percent to the eighteen-month column (31 December 2027; 43.7 percent annualised; a value of SEK 65.46) and +80.9 percent to the three-year column (30 June 2029; 24.7 percent annualised; SEK 76.93). The model's template splits the eighteen-month return into earnings +48.4 percent, dividends +3.2 percent and the multiple +1.6 percent. The template overstates the earnings leg, and its inputs predate this memo's changes (see the end notes); on our changed base, the eighteen-month return at 19.93x is about +50 percent.

The return re-stated like for like, on our changed base, at the four multiples that matter. The 24-month-forward EPS that the price capitalises today is about SEK 2.61 on our base (a blend of FY2027 and FY2028), so the multiple today on our earnings is about 16.3x. At the eighteen-month column the shares are valued on FY2029 EPS (about SEK 3.13) plus SEK 1.20 of dividends (SEK 0.50 for FY2026 and SEK 0.70 for FY2027). At the three-year column they are valued on a blend of FY2030 and FY2031 EPS (about SEK 3.66) plus SEK 2.10 of dividends.

On consensus earnings at 14x (with FY2029 EPS projected at about SEK 3.69 from FY2028's SEK 3.42), the eighteen-month return is about +25 percent, or about 21 percent a year. That is the return the market is implicitly underwriting.

What drives the return. Earnings do all the work in the return, and they are not in dispute at the EBITA line; the multiple is where our case and the market's diverge.

  • Earnings: the earnings leg is +20 percent over eighteen months and +40 percent over three years on our numbers, but only about +13 and +25 percent on the market's numbers, because the market already capitalises a higher starting EPS.
  • Multiple: from 16.3x on our earnings, every plausible exit multiple below 16.5x is a de-rating, and the guideline's 19.9x is the only path to the framework's 20 percent-a-year bar at three years.
  • Dividends: dividends add about 2 percent a year, and the February dividend decision puts even that at risk.

The price at which our 14x path returns 20 percent a year over eighteen months is about SEK 36 (about SEK 40 on consensus earnings), which is also where the previous memo's buy level sat.

The buy level: at about SEK 36, our 14x path returns 20 percent a year over eighteen months.

Where I differ from the market. The market's return case needs the brokers' EPS, not ours, and a multiple at or above today's. My return case needs the multiple to hold at the 75th percentile of the stock's own history for a balance sheet whose acquisition engine is off. Neither is the most likely path. The most likely path is a mid-single-digit return over eighteen months within a wide range of outcomes: -35 to -40 percent at a 10x trough multiple on our earnings, and about +27 percent at 16.5x on consensus earnings.

Score: 35. A low modal return at a defensible multiple, with the attractive branch requiring either the brokers' below-EBITA chain to be right or a multiple the company earned only in 2020 to 2021.

13 Summary conclusion on the business and its investment case

Instalco is a good operating recovery attached to a stretched balance sheet, priced for the recovery and not yet for the balance sheet.

The operating half is doing what the founder said it would. Sweden is back at a 7.4 percent margin in a weak quarter; group adjusted EBITA in Q3 was about a third above a year earlier, on volume returning to a pruned base; Fabri has arrived at a 12 percent margin; and the method (selective bidding, a baseline of standards, country accountability) has now held for five quarters. That half of the case is strong, predictable to within a few percent and, in our view, skewed to the upside against our own model.

The balance-sheet half, which the Q3 report put in front of the market on 23 October, has four parts:

  • Growth at Instalco consumes cash.
  • The debt-funded purchase of 51 percent of Fabri and SEK 200m of minority buy-outs in one quarter took leverage from 2.6x to 3.3x, in a hiking cycle.
  • The cash that the acquisition engine needs will not be available before the end of 2027.
  • The per-share earnings the market capitalises carry a chain of interest, minorities and tax that the three brokers model about SEK 0.35 to 0.40 too lightly for 2027.

The multiple sits at the stock's own-history median on the brokers' earnings and at the 75th percentile on ours; the 19.9x guideline belongs to a different era of this company.

The practical conclusion for Richard. For the next six to nine months the fundamental outcomes are skewed positive at EBITA but negative at EPS and cash. The probability of guidance and sell-side upgrades, which is what Richard looks for, is therefore unusually low here until the February 2027 report, not unusually high. The case to own the shares existed at SEK 21 to 30 in early 2026, and that return has been collected. The case to own them again is dated and specific: either a price near SEK 36, or a Q4 2026 report (11 February 2027) showing rolling cash conversion back above 90 percent, a working-capital release of SEK 400m or more and pro forma leverage at or below 2.7x. That report would move the acquisition restart back to H2 2027 and re-open the engine-on multiple. Until then, expect operating beats, EPS cuts and unchanged guidance, from a stock that must keep beating operationally just to hold its price.

Thesis's Change Forces' Strength: B. Five internal forces acting at once, under a founder who owns 8.56 percent of the equity, have delivered five quarters of margin recovery ahead of plan in a genuine Nordic cyclical upturn. The acquisition engine is off and the cash leg has reversed, which keeps the grade out of the A band.

Foundations' Robustness: C. The margin recovery rests on the company's own demonstrated history and on an industry that rewards disciplined consolidators. But the moat is relational and not widening, there is no pricing power in tenders, return on capital employed is 9.6 percent, goodwill is 145 percent of equity and leverage is 3.3x in a hiking cycle.

Setups' Fit/Crispness: C. The case fits the framework's "Big Corporate Change-driven EPS upgrade" (EPSU) setup. The setup is crisp at EBITA (margin from 6.0 to 7.2 percent in a year) but blurred at EPS and cash (a 40 to 45 percent leak below EBITA, and cash conversion of 74 percent). The case does not fit three other setups: it is not a "CfC Clearing" (the multiple has already recovered to the median), not a trough-on-trough cyclical (the multiple is mid-range), and not a mechanical serial-acquirer upgrader (the acquisition engine is off until 2028).

Case Riskiness: D. The case is simple to state but not low-risk. Four correlated roll-up risks (write-down, cash, leverage and dilution) are live rather than latent after Q3; consensus EPS cuts are more likely than not at the next three events; the stock is a levered Swedish small cap with a company-driven multiple whose five-year range is 7.9x to 34x; and the downside to a trough multiple on our earnings is about 35 percent.
